clue.text: Working hours fixed by such enchanting folk, on paper

blocks.note: The Times, the newspaper this crossword appears in
people who cast spells

explanation.surface: Office hours set by a coven of witches and written down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-reading charade 'on' would mean below; in this across entry the newspaper simply comes first, with the spell-casters placed beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Time switches are clock devices that turn heating or lights on and off at set hours, so they fix when things are working.

clue.text: Naming bird and fish

blocks.note: a small songbird, as in blue tit
a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Identifying a bird and a fish, as a naturalist might.
explanation.definitionFit: Titling something means giving it a title, which is a way of naming it.

clue.text: Sells fantasy film, cutting dirty bits

indicators.note: one thing cutting into another sits inside it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: E.T., Spielberg's film about an alien
stains or smudges

explanation.surface: A distributor sells a fantasy film after editing out the rude scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty bits' suggests censored footage, but it means marks, as in grubby spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To market goods is to promote and sell them, so markets is a verb synonym of sells.

clue.text: Here top candidates, found lacking, go to one side

blocks.note: short of something means lacking it
a ship lists when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: The best applicants, judged inadequate, are pushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the answer: the place where the top candidates appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the final selection of best applicants from which a winner is chosen, so it is where top candidates are found.

clue.text: Madagascan climber some find ridiculous

indicators.note: some of the following words means just part of their run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words

explanation.surface: A mountaineer from Madagascar whom some people find absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a tree-climbing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is the largest living lemur, native to Madagascar, and lives in the trees.

clue.text: Collapse with strain during competition

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to rack is to stretch or strain
a cup is a knockout tournament, as in the FA Cup

explanation.surface: An athlete breaks down under pressure in the middle of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack-up is a mental or physical breakdown, the noun sense of collapse.

clue.text: Typical example I included in record book

indicators.note: something included in a collection goes inside it, so one piece is placed within the others

blocks.note: taken as written
an extended-play record
a large heavy book

explanation.surface: A fine specimen listed in the Guinness Book of Records, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative of a type, the classic example of it.

clue.text: Associate originally telling story that several may draw on?

indicators.note: originally points to how the word begins, so only its opening letter counts

blocks.note: to associate with a group is to join it
its first letter
an account is a narrative of events

explanation.surface: A storyteller's tale that a group of artists might sketch from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw on' sounds like artists or writers using a story for inspiration; here it means withdrawing money.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint bank account is shared by two or more holders, each of whom may withdraw funds from it.

clue.text: Working group of small proportions fencing area in province

indicators.note: fencing something encloses it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a group of only three is small
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A small working party puts a fence round a patch of land in a province.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is one of the provinces of Canada, home to Toronto and Ottawa.

clue.text: Taking out illustration

blocks.note: first meaning: withdrawing, as money from a bank or a sword from its sheath
second meaning: a picture made with pencil or pen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking out' reads like removing a picture from a book; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing is both the act of pulling something out and a sketched picture.

clue.text: Good surgeon with time for disguise becomes hard to find

indicators.note: a disguise changes the appearance, so these letters are rearranged beyond recognition

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A capable surgeon takes time to adopt a disguise and vanishes from view.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'Good surgeon' plus the time letter is the fodder; 'Good' looks like the usual G abbreviation but is used in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to ground is an idiom from hunting, where a fox hides in its earth, meaning to hide away.

clue.text: Most gullible Scot brought back waistcoat from US

indicators.note: brought back means returned the way it came, so the name is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Ian is a typical Scottish first name
Americans call a waistcoat a vest

explanation.surface: A trusting Scotsman returns with an American waistcoat, having been duped.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a vest is an undershirt; the US sense, a waistcoat, is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and easily fooled, and the superlative naivest means most easily taken in.

clue.text: Trying to reform smoker, I must take the lead

indicators.note: reforming something remakes it in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged
taking the lead means going in front, so this piece is placed at the start

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting a smoker to quit is hard work, and I must lead the effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like a verb, attempting, but it is the adjective meaning annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome means irritating or tiresome, the adjective sense of trying.

clue.text: Protection from extremely aggressive soldiers

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its two ends, which are the letters kept

blocks.note: its first and last letters
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Seeking protection from soldiers who are very hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for aggressive; it asks for that word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the aegis of someone means under their protection, from the shield of Zeus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Developing public disturbance in which Democrat becomes sanctimonious

indicators.note: one thing that becomes another is swapped out for it, so a letter is replaced

blocks.note: an incident is a violent public disturbance
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
pi is short for pious, meaning sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A political row breaks out in which a Democrat starts sounding preachy.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is British slang for pious or sanctimonious; it takes the place of the Democrat's D.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipient means just beginning to appear, in an early stage of developing.

clue.text: Partner set up first-rate business groups

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means raised, so the term is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a consort is a spouse or companion
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A partner launches several top-quality companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia, plural of consortium, are associations of companies working together on a venture.

clue.text: Native repelled by daily fraud

indicators.note: something repelled is pushed back, so the word for native is turned round

blocks.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
natal means relating to birth, as in one's native land

explanation.surface: A local resident is turned away by a newspaper that is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests a newspaper, but here it is a cleaner. The reversed word sits after it, being 'repelled by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a person who falsely claims special skill, a fraud or impostor.

clue.text: Redcoat's re-dressed, 30's style

indicators.note: dressed again in different clothing, so these letters are rearranged into a new outfit

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A British soldier's uniform is restyled in a fashion of the 1930s.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcoat was a British soldier, or a Butlin's holiday-camp host; the word is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s, with bold geometric forms.

clue.text: Like song racily composed by learner?

indicators.note: something composed is put together in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
L is for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Is it a song a beginner wrote in a risqué style?
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical describes something with the expressive, musical quality of a song.

clue.text: Host runs off in very skimpy underwear

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a host is a large crowd
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A party host makes a dash for it wearing nothing but scanty underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the person throwing a party; it is the multitude sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is minimal underwear with a narrow strip at the back.

clue.text: Boundary of either kind in test is commonplace

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another word

blocks.note: a cricket boundary scores four or six runs, IV or VI in Roman numerals
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Edges of every sort in an exam are routine.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a four or a six; either works, since TR+IV+IAL and TRI+VI+AL give the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means ordinary and unimportant, much like commonplace.

clue.text: Head of obstetrics to register closure of busy hospital department

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is kept
closure means the end, so the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: its first letter
taken as written
a log is a record or register
its last letter

explanation.surface: A senior obstetrician records the closure of a busy hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'closure' reads as shutting a department; it only asks for the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Otology is the medical study and treatment of the ear, a specialty with its own hospital department.

clue.text: Complete sentence child finally spoke

indicators.note: finally points to the end of each word, so only last letters are kept

blocks.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense
its last letter
its last letter

explanation.surface: A toddler at last speaks a whole sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' serves both sentence and child, taking the last letter of each.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter words is to speak them, so uttered is the past tense matching spoke.

clue.text: Senior member's wish to support party

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means lying underneath, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: a do is a party or celebration
a yen is a longing or wish

explanation.surface: A veteran club member hopes to back a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics but means a social do. The 's in member's stands for has, linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving person in a group or profession.

clue.text: Foreign banker's gold in old firm

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An overseas financier keeps his gold in a long-established company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword favourite for a river, something with banks, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major South American river flowing through Venezuela, a foreign one with banks.

clue.text: Almost every line judge pens becomes cloying

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
to pen something is to shut it in an enclosure, so one piece holds the others

blocks.note: to try a case is to judge it
each means every
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A line judge who writes nearly every call turns sickly sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line judge' looks like a tennis official, but the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacly means like treacle, the British name for molasses or golden syrup, so excessively sweet and sentimental.

clue.text: Old hat said to irritate hard patch of skin

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to try someone is to tax their patience
a corn is a hard lump of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: An outdated hat rubs against a corn on the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like the idiom for something stale; it means a historical hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat of the eighteenth century, so literally an old hat.

clue.text: Possibly a dish for Long John's sports venue?

blocks.note: a bowl is a dish
a dish meant for a kitchen is kept in it
Long John Silver, the ship's cook in Treasure Island, works in a galley, a ship's kitchen

explanation.surface: A pirate cook's dish turns up in a ten-pin venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as BOWL IN GALLEY: a dish in the cook's kitchen. Long John Silver was the ship's cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling alley is a building with lanes for ten-pin bowling, a sports venue.
